answer: Admission requires staking a velvet bond that is released only after the applicant completes a growing trellis of unpaid tasks, each assigned by a different established peer and checked against a public prism of operator fingerprints such as key-use timing and hardware attestation. If two identities share an operator, their fingerprints coincide in the prism and both velvet bonds are slashed. Until the trellis is fully signed, emissions cannot be withdrawn, so a farm cannot mint many full shares from one wallet.
